ORDINANCE NO. 010697-2
ORDINANCE OF CITY OF MONTICELLO
BE IT ORDAINED by the mayor and council of the City of Monticello in council duly assembled, and it is hereby ordained by the authority of same that the authority, right, permission and consent are hereby granted to Central Georgia EMC, it successors, lessees and assigns (the "company'), subject to the terms and conditions set forth hereinafter for a period of 35 years, to occupy and use the streets, alleys and public places of the City of Monticello (the "city") within the present and future limits of the city as from time to time the company may deem proper or necessary for the overhead or underground construction, maintenance, operation and extension of poles, towers, lines, wires, cables, conduits, insulators, transformers, appliances, equipment, connections and other apparatus for the business and purpose of transmitting, conveying, conducting, using, supplying and distributing electricity for light, heat, power and other purposes for which electric current may be or become useful or practicable for public or private use, and to reenter upon such streets, alleys and public places from time to time as the company may deem proper or necessary to perform these functions, and to cut and trim trees and shrubbery when and where necessary, in the judgement of the company, to ensure safe and efficient service.
BE IT FURTHER ORDAINED, that from and after the adoption of this ordinance, the future use by C.G. EMC of the streets, alleys, public places and other property of the city for the operation of C.G. EMC's electric distribution systems, and the grant of the requisite street franchise rights, is expressly conditioned upon payment of franchise fees pursuant to this ordinance, and continued use and occupancy of such city property for said purpose without payment of such franchise fees shall be unlawful, and the city shall be entitled to enforce compliance with this ordinance by appropriate proceeding at law or in equity.
BE IT FURTHER ORDAINED, that the rights, permission and consents herein contained are made for the following considerations and upon the following terms and conditions, to wit:
1. The company shall pay to the city:
(a) On or before the first day of March, 1997, a sum of money equal to four percent of the gross sales of electric energy to all of the company's customers served within the corporate limits of the city during the period beginning on the first day of January, 1997, through and including December 31, 1997; and
(b) On or before the first day of March, 1998, and the same day or each year thereafter during the term of the franchise herein granted a sum of money equal to four percent of the gross sales of electric energy to all of the company's customers served within the corporate limits of this city during the preceding calendar year;
provided, however, that in the event the city shall grant to any other electric utility the right to use and occupy its streets for like purposes, such use and occupancy shall be upon the same terms and conditions as those herein contained, including the payment provisions hereof.
2. The amount, if any, of any tax, fee, charge or imposition of any kind required, demanded or exacted by the city on any account, other than ad valorem taxes on property and license taxes on the sale of home appliances, shall operate to reduce to the extent of such tax, fee, charge or imposition the amount due from the percentage of gross sales as provided herein at paragraph 1.
3. The company shall fully protect, indemnify and save harmless the city from all damages to person or property caused by the construction, maintenance, operation or extension or poles, wires or other apparatus or conditions of streets, alleys or public places resulting therefrom, for which the said city would otherwise be liable.
4. The company shall, in constructing, maintaining, operating and extending its poles, wires and other apparatus, submit and be subject to all reasonable exercises of the police power by the city. Nothing contained herein, however, shall require the company to surrender or limit is property rights created hereby without due process of law, including adequate compensation, for any other purposes at the instance of the city or for any purpose at the instance of any other entity, private or governmental.
5. The grant of the rights, permission and consents by the city to the company contained in this ordinance are specifically conditioned upon the payment of all sums due the city in accordance with the rate, conditions and payment dates set forth in paragraph 1, above, and failure by the company to timely pay the franchise fees required by said paragraph 1 shall constitute a forfeiture of all rights granted by this ordinance. From and after January 1, 1997, the company's continued use and occupancy of the streets, alleys and public places of the city for the aforesaid purposes shall evidence the company's acceptance of the franchise granted hereby and shall render the company liable for payment of all fees required by paragraph 1 hereof. In the event of a forfeiture for failure to comply with such requirements, the company shall nevertheless remain liable for all sums accrued until such time as the streets are vacated due to such forfeiture.
This ordinance shall be effective as of 1 January, 1997. All ordinances and parts of ordinances in conflict herewith shall be and the same are hereby replaced.

ORDINANCE NO. 98-10-13-2
THE CITY OF MONTICELLO HEREBY ORDAINS:
Sec. 1. That Williams Communications, Inc., referred to herein as licensee, is hereby authorized to encroach upon the public right of way in certain streets and alleys in the City of Monticello, for the purpose of installing, constructing, operating, maintaining, repairing, and removing a fiber-optic telecommunications system to provide long distance network services, shown as solid lines on a plan prepared by licensee. The initial term of this ordinance shall be for 20 years, beginning as of the effective date herein, and licensee shall have the right to renew the license on the same terms and conditions expressed herein for two successive ten-year periods.
Sec. 2. This ordinance authorizes licensee to encroach upon the public right-of-way as set forth on such drawing only to traverse the city, as requested by the licensee. The licensee shall give the city 30 days' advance written notice requesting any additional use of right-of-way and shall abide by any permitting requirements as specified by city ordinances. The city and licensee have agreed that the ordinance does not authorize the provision of any service in the city and that the provision of services shall require separate authorization from the city.
Sec. 3. The rights granted by this ordinance to the licensee are personal to the licensee (as currently owned and controlled) and shall not be assigned or transferred, directly or indirectly, without the prior written consent of the city.
Sec. 4. The grant of authorization for the above-described encroachment shall also be subject to the following specific conditions:
(a) The licensee, or any successor or assign, shall bear all costs incurred in connection with the installation, construction maintenance, repair, operation and removal of the encroachments.
(b) The licensee, on licensee's own behalf and on behalf of any successor or assign, shall acknowledge and assume all responsibility for the permitted use of public right-of-way and the installation, construction, maintenance, repair, operation and removal of the encroachments, which shall be undertaken without risk or liability on the part of the city.
(c) Within 30 days from the effective date of this ordinance, licensee shall pay a lump sum fee for the initial term of the ordinance equal to an annual fee of $1.50 per linear foot of cable in the public right-of-way (20 × $1.50 × X number of feet). This fee shall be adjusted for each subsequent renewal term based upon the percentage change in the consumer price index (CPI) between the effective date of the previous term and the renewal date.
(d) The licensee shall furnish the city evidence of a public liability insurance contract in an amount of $1,000,000.00 combined single limit, naming the city as an additional insured.
(e) The licensee shall require any contractor or contractors to furnish the city evidence of a public liability and property damage insurance contract in an amount of $1,000,000.00 combined single limit, naming the city as an additional insured.
Sec. 5. The licensee shall be responsible and must bear all cost for repair of any damage or movement of the encroachments and/or to the structure the encroachment is attached to due to repair, maintenance and/or failure/collapse of the existing gas, water and sewer lines under or approximately under said encroachment.
Sec. 6. The licensee shall place cables underground where required to do so and in any other locations where required by the city manager.
Sec. 7. Prior to construction a final location plan shall be submitted for approval by the city manager, and the city manager shall be authorized to permit or to require all alternate location for the proposed conduit within the public right-of-way to avoid conflict with other permitted uses or to establish an appropriate width from curb for placement of conduit for the use proposed.
Sec. 8. The licensee shall provide as-built drawings detailing the location of fiber optic conduits and manholes installed pursuant to the authorization.
Sec. 9. This ordinance shall be in force upon adoption and shall become effective when the licensee furnishes the required insurance and bond forms and files a written statement in form satisfactory to the city attorney to the effect that the licensee agrees to be bound by and to comply with the terms and conditions upon which the encroachment authorization is granted.
This ordinance becomes effective the 13th day of October, 1998.
